The petitioner has sought quashing of notification dated 7.2.2008 (Annexure P-5), notification dated 6.2.2009 (Annexure P-7), award dated 4.2.2021 (Annexure P-17) and the order dated 19.10.2022 (Annexure P-31).
2.

On 19.12.2022, the learned State counsel stated that owing to inadvertence the impugned order dated 19.10.2022 (Annexure P-31) has been shown to have been passed, whereas, infact, the matter is still pending consideration with the Zonal Administrator, Urban Estate, Panchkula.
3. Today, the learned Addl. Advocate General, Haryana has placed on record the speaking order.
The speaking order was passed on the recommendation of the Zonal Committee.

Upon such recommendation, the Chief Administrator, (Town Planning Wing) HSVP, Panchkula made the Gokal vs State Of Haryana And Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109482766/

sentences.text: following recommendations:-
"In continuation to this office letter No.6797-6800 dated 11.7.2018 and 8111-12 dated 30.8.2018, the recommendations of this office is as under:

Since the possession of the land in question has been taken over by HSVP vide rapat rojnamcha no.503 dated 4.2.2011 and the land is affecting 01 nos. institutional plot of fire station and side of police station of Sector 76, Faridabad, it is not recommended to release the land of petition."
4. In pursuance of the above recommendations, the matter was finally considered by the competent authority and it was concluded as under:-
"Conclusion

In view of the above, the recommendations of this office [based on reports of LAO (Faridabad) DTP (Faridabad)] have been approved by the Competent Authority i.e. Govt. of haryana, whose decision has been conveyed vide letter memo No. A-7- 2022/7799 dated 26.12.2022 and accordingly, the present representation is rejected as the land in question is duly planned and is required for public purpose of Site of Fire Station and Police Station as per layout of Sector 76, Faridabad

, hence orders of Hon'ble High Court are complied with dated 11.5.2015 in CWP No.
9194/2015."
5. However, the said speaking order has been challenged by the writ petitioner.

6. The argument raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner for making a challenge to the said order, is founded on the premise, that the petition lands, as became put to acquisition, rather also required to be de- notified, as they are now, in terms of Section 101 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation & Resettlement Act, 2013' (for short 'the Act of 2013'), as added through an authenticity of this order/judgement CWP No. 29310 of 2022 -3- 2023:PHHC:089715-DB amendment made by the Haryana State Legislative Assembly in 2018, provisions whereof are extracted hereinafter, thus unviable or non-essential for becoming put to the relevant public purpose.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, for the reasons to be assigned hereinafter, the above made argument is completely rudderless, and, is rejected.
"101. Return of unutilised land.

When any land acquired under this Act remains unutilised for a period of five years from the date of taking over the possession, the same shall be returned to the original owner or owners or their legal heirs, as the case may be, or to the Land Bank of the appropriate Government by reversion in the manner as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government."

sentences.text: A perusal of the speaking order (supra) reveals, that the award in respect of the acquired lands was pronounced on 4.2.2011, and, also apparently possession of the acquired land became assumed by the respondent, thus resulting in vestment of the right, title and interest over the acquired lands on the respondent-State, and, obviously also resulting in divestment of right, title and interest of the present petitioners rather over the acquired lands.

Significantly, since it has also been depicted in the said order, that compensation in respect of the land, has been disbursed to the present petitioner, but though compensation also became determined in respect of the structures raised thereons, but yet the said determined amount of compensation, rather remains unclaimed,
therefore, it remains undisbursed to the present petitioner.

8. Therefore, if the present petitioner has acquiesced to the making of the said award, besides even if he was aggrieved by any deficit amount of compensation, thus becoming assessed not only in respect of the lands, as became put to acquisition but also in respect of the structures, if any, as authenticity of this order/judgement CWP No. 29310 of 2022 -4- 2023:PHHC:089715-DB became raised thereons.

Resultantly, it was open for the petitioner to raise a petition claiming enhancement of the compensation, thus before the Collector concerned, for the latter thereafter forwarding it, to the Reference Court concerned, for a determination, being made thereons hence by the learned Reference Court concerned.
However, it has not been done.
Therefore, the award of the Collector concerned, does acquire a conclusive, and, binding effect.

9. Even otherwise, even if assumingly in terms of the above extracted amendment, as made by the State of Haryana, to the Act of 2013, the acquired land, though, at this stage, becomes purportedly unviable or non essential, thereby though may purportedly become amenable for being de- notified from acquisition, yet since it has been clearly spoken in the order, made on the representation of the petitioner, that the acquired lands are necessary for facilitating the public purpose, as an institutional plot for a fire-station, and, site of police station, as becomes raised thereons.

Therefore,
but obviously the said speakings, rather make the acquired lands to be even now both viable, and,
essential for thus being subjected to use for the apposite public purpose.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the petitioner cannot argue, that as of now, the acquired lands are unviable or non essential for acquisition, and, thereby they be released from acquisition.

10. The learned counsel for the petitioner has yet continued to argue, that the respondent-State has indulged in hostile discrimination, inasmuch as, it taking to decline the writ claim to the present petitioner, whereas, its proceeding to release the other acquired land, merely to facilitate the builders concerned, who purchased such lands, thus to raise constructions thereons.
authenticity of this order/judgement
However, even the above made argument is not amenable for CWP No. 29310 of 2022 -5- 2023:PHHC:089715-DB becoming accepted by this Court.

The reason is but simple, that if the said ground was to be raised, it was required to be raised in Civil Writ Petition No. 9194 of 2015, whereas, its not being raised, thus attracts against the said extantly raised averment, the estopping principle, as becomes engrafted in Order II Rule 2 of the CPC, provisions whereof become extracted hereinafter, whereby in the event of any fact, though required to be set up or pleaded, at the first instance, thus remaining unpleaded, thereupon there is an estoppel against its being impleaded subsequently, as has been untenably done in the present writ petition.

2. Suit to include the whole claim-- (1) Every suit shall include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entitled to make in respect of the cause of action; but a plaintiff may relinquish any portion of his claim in order to bring the suit within the jurisdiction of any Court.

(2)
Relinquishment of part of claim--Where a plaintiff omits to sue in respect of, or intentionally relinquishes, any portion of his claim he shall not afterwards sue in respect of the portion so omitted or relinquished.

(3) Omission to sue for one of several reliefs--A person entitled to more than one relief in respect of the same cause of action may sue for all or any of such reliefs; but if he omits, except with the leave of the Court, to sue for all such reliefs, he shall not afterwards sue for any relief so omitted.
Explanation--For the purposes of this rule an obligation and a collateral security for its performance and successive claims arising under the same obligation shall be deemed respectively to constitute but one cause of action."
12.

Even otherwise, it is within the domain of objective contemplation of the respondent-State to deem it fit, and, appropriate to utilize or make viable, besides declare essential any acquired lands,
and, to also declare other acquired lands, thus within the terms of the said statutory GURPREET SINGH 2023.07.25 12:17

I attest to the accuracy andprovisions rather to be unessential or unviable for relevant public purpose, authenticity of this order/judgement Chandigarh CWP No. 29310 of 2022 -6- 2023:PHHC:089715-DB and, thereby may proceed to release such acquired lands from acquisition.

Therefore, unless there are proven malafides on the part of the respondent- State,
thereupon, the above said objective contemplation, as made by the respondent-State, cannot be interfered by this Court.

Since, as above stated, the petitioner has been paid compensation, and,
thereby acquiesced to the making(s) of the award, besides when there is no material, adduced on record by the petitioner, suggestive that the acquired lands are to be not used or nor being used for the institutional purposes (supra), thereby also the petitioner cannot argue, but on the above parity,
that thereby hostile discrimination, has been perpetrated on him, nor he can argue that the acquired lands rather be released from acquisition nor he can also argue, that the impugned order be quashed, and, set aside.
13.
In view of the above, there is no merit in the petition, and, the same is hereby dismissed.
(SURESHWAR THAKUR) JUDGE (KULDEEP TIWARI) JUDGE July 18, 2023 Gurpreet/Ajay Kumar
